scope: A download manager for the web, a Notepad menu, simpler main menu keys, and Control+F1 for the main menu.

topics.title: Download manager
details: When you choose a download link, you hear Downloading and the file name. You hear again when it is done.
Press Control+D on a web page to open Downloads. It is also in the Web browser menu.
Use Up and Down to move through your downloads. A file that is still coming says how far along it is.
Space pauses or resumes. Delete cancels. Control+Up and Control+Down move a waiting download earlier or later.
Enter opens a finished file. Sound and video play in the media player. Documents open in the reader.
Escape goes back to the page where you were.
Files go to your Downloads folder. You can pick another folder in Web browser options.
This works the same in Chrome and in the built-in browser.
If you use Chrome, open the Voice Companion extension card and choose Reload.

topics.title: Notepad menu
details: Notepad now opens to its own menu. It has Create a note, Open a note, Options, and Main menu.
Control+N creates a note. Control+O opens one. Alt+O opens options.
Escape in a note saves it and goes back to this menu.

topics.title: Control+F1 goes to the main menu
details: Press Control+F1 on any screen to go to the main menu.
Print Screen takes screenshots again, as usual in Windows.

topics.title: Main menu keys
details: Control+V says the version. Control+M says the speech mode.
Control+G opens the user guide. Control+T starts the tutorial.
The old keys with Shift still work.

topics.title: Web and email
details: A heading that is also a link now says so. For example: JAWS downloads, heading level 3, link.
Links and buttons in email sound the same as on the web.
A link you open from an email goes to the browser you chose in Web browser options.
An email address link starts a new email to that address.

topics.title: Microphone and time
details: F9 off is now remembered when you close Voice Companion. At start, you hear that it is off.
The time is said in words, such as two forty-six PM or three oh seven AM.
In the media player, Alt no longer says this screen has no Alt menu.
